descriptions.text: Enchanted Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly. There’s a children’s story out there about a dragonfly who gets so drunk that his wife won’t let him come home, so he hovers in the air above their nest, waiting for her to go to sleep, so he can get to bed. The thing is, the wife knows he’s out there, and she ain’t moving. So the dragonfly either hovers all night or moves to the highest point, sitting on a leaf, overlooking his home, waiting for his wife to turn the light back on to signify he’s out of the doghouse. This tiara has been made to honor that poor Dragonfly with the angry wife. …

recap.text: Donut hovers two feet off the ground in the Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly, whose large citrine is not her colour. The gnome jeweler at the Desperado Club set it for 25,000 gold. She will wear a dead man's sailor hat until her cards run out. When Carl learns Lucia means to kill her and her pet dinosaur, Donut casts Hover to show off, and Carl bites back his scolding.

A box gives Donut a second charging pillow, purple to go with the red one. Grumbling, she sets her new boonie hat on the red pillow and the Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly on the other, and each clicks. She wants her Hover, which is part of the tiara, back on, but Mordecai thinks it is not worth it, since her skills run to thousands. Okay, she sniffs.

beats.headline: The citrine, set at last
beats.text: Donut is walking on air, two feet off the ground, on the fourth Hover of the day. Her Flawless Jeweler's Gem is a large citrine, not her colour. They have kept her Tiara of Mana Genita and bought a blank tiara from the gnome jeweler at the Desperado Club; it took her twenty minutes to pick a simple silver-coloured one, and 25,000 gold to have the jewel installed. Her dislike of the colour ended with the description: half the potion cooldown, ten intelligence, no dexterity debuff when drunk, and a level-10 Hover, five a day for about ninety seconds, a dollar-store version of Elle's.
beats.gist: Donut hovers two feet up, her citrine set in a silver tiara for 25,000 gold.

beats.headline: Off, for the sailor hat
beats.text: Wearing a dead man's sailor hat means giving up her new Hover skill and ten intelligence, Carl points out. Donut has already talked to Mordecai about it: she will wear the hat until she runs out of cards, then put her new dragonfly tiara back on. The hat lowers the draw countdown by two seconds, and it is quite jaunty.
beats.gist: Donut will wear the sailor hat until her cards run out, then return to the tiara.

beats.headline: Showing off the Hover
beats.text: Carl has just learned in chat that Lucia means to kill Donut and her pet dinosaur on the next floor, and he looks nervously at Donut. She is standing on the edge of Tran's flying wheelchair module, and she laughs with delight, switches into her dragonfly tiara, and casts Hover to show them all her new skill. Carl holds himself back from chiding her for wasting a five-times-a-day skill. Tran smiles and pets her.
beats.gist: Donut laughs, switches into her dragonfly tiara and casts Hover on Tran's flying wheelchair module.

beats.headline: On the purple pillow
beats.text: A box gives Donut a second charging pillow, purple instead of red: it drains any magical item, but transfers only to a like item. Mordecai wants hats draining before they move on. Grumbling, Donut sets the pillows on the counter, her new boonie hat on the red one and the Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly on the other, and each clicks as it touches. When talk turns to which of her spells and skills Quan's cloak might raise to fifteen, she remembers that her Hover is part of the dragonfly tiara and wants it back on. Hover would not be worth it, Mordecai thinks, and her pool of skills runs to thousands anyway. Okay, she sniffs.
beats.gist: Donut sets her hat and tiara on the two pillows; Mordecai says Hover isn't worth it.

relations.note: the blank tiara came from its gnome jeweller
